title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1969-01-26

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 1969 show with standout Eleven → Lovelight and a clean, well‑balanced matrix recording despite occasional mix quirks
ai_review.review: The performance is praised for its manic intensity – the eleven‑minute “The Eleven” into an epic “Lovelight”, a soaring “Clementine”, and a gut‑wrenching “Death Don't Have No Mercy” are repeatedly highlighted.  The recording, taken from early 16‑track (matrix) sources, is generally clear and well balanced (Jerry’s guitar and Pigpen’s organ sit nicely), though several reviewers note treble‑muddy spots and brief mix fluctuations.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews are 4–5 stars, emphasizing exceptional musical moments and a mostly good recording; only a few note mix problems, so the overall weighted rating is high.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear overall balance with Jerry’s guitar and Pigpen’s organ well captured; occasional treble‑muddy character and brief mix fluctuations noted by several reviewers.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Reviewers describe the set as flowing naturally from high‑energy jams into tightly linked sequences (e.g., Clementine → Dark Horse → St. Stephen), with a particularly inspired second half.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for tearing up his Gibson, delivering a powerful solo on “Lovelight” and an intense, fast‑paced short Dark Star; his tone is described as clean and masterful.
band_member_comments.Phil: Repeatedly called a ‘beast’; highlighted for a bass line reminiscent of “So What” in Clementine and overall strong, creative playing throughout.
band_member_comments.Bob: Mentioned only indirectly (“Bobby hitting Spoonful”) – no specific guitar/vocal critique.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ is noted as well recorded and balanced; one reviewer wonders about Tom C.’s presence, indicating the organ sound stands out.
